subtitle: At Warangal’s Rings of Earth and Stone, a King Chooses Survival Over Glory

panels.shot: epic wide from above the fort, concentric walls encircled by vast armies
panels.action: Prataparudra II stands on the inner stone rampart of Warangal, granite towers behind him, watching distant Delhi banners gather around the outer earthen wall like a tightening noose.

dialogue.text: In 1310, at Warangal’s granite walls, King Prataparudra faced Malik Kafur’s northern storm—and chose tribute over ruin to keep his realm alive.

i18n.hi: १३१० में, वरंगल की ग्रेनाइट दीवारों पर, राजा प्रतापरुद्र ने मलिक काफ़ूर की उत्तरी आँधी देखी—और राज्य बचाने को खंडणी चुनी, विनाश नहीं

panels.shot: slow push-in toward Prataparudra on the ramparts at dawn
panels.action: Prataparudra II, armored but bare-headed, leans on the crenellations of the inner stone fort as the first light touches dry tanks and fields beyond, his face tense yet composed.

dialogue.text: Delhi’s armies had never come this far. Yet in early 1310, Malik Kafur’s march reached Warangal, drawn by the Kakatiyas’ elephants, horses and hidden wealth.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली की फ़ौजें कभी इतनी दूर नहीं आई थीं। पर १३१० की शुरुआत में मलिक काफ़ूर की चढ़ाई वरंगल तक पहुँची, काकतीयों के हाथी, घोड़े और छुपे ख़ज़ाने के पीछे

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Deccan landscape with marching host in the distance
panels.action: Across a dusty Deccan plain, long columns of soldiers, pack animals and horsemen snake forward under fluttering Khalji standards, heat haze shimmering above them.

dialogue.text: Amir Khusrau tells us Alauddin Khalji ordered the march in late 1309. Months later, Kafur’s army crossed rivers and rocky plains to stand before Warangal.

i18n.hi: अमीर ख़ुसरो लिखते हैं कि अलाउद्दीन खिलज़ी ने चढ़ाई का हुक्म १३๐९ के अंत में दिया। कुछ महीने बाद, काफ़ूर की सेना नदियाँ और पथरीले मैदान पार कर वरंगल के सामने आ खड़ी हुई

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view revealing the concentric defenses of Warangal
panels.action: From high above, Warangal’s outer ring of hardened earth curves around fields and habitations, while the inner stone fortress rises within, encircled by a dark moat.

dialogue.text: Warangal was not a single wall. It was rings of defense—an outer hardened mud circuit, and within it, a stone bastion with moat, much as Khusrau described and stones still show.

i18n.hi: वरंगल कोई एक दीवार नहीं था। ये थे घेरदार किले—बाहर सख़्त मिट्टी का घेरा, भीतर पत्थर का किला और खाई, जैसा ख़ुसरो ने लिखा और जैसा पत्थर आज भी दिखाते हैं

panels.shot: medium shot on Prataparudra in council hall, lit by oil lamps
panels.action: Inside a pillared hall, Prataparudra sits on a low throne, surrounded by advisors and generals, palm-leaf maps of the fort’s rings spread before them.

dialogue.text: Prataparudra had ruled for years over a rich, irrigated kingdom. Diamond-bearing tracts and temple treasuries made Warangal tempting prey for the cash-hungry Delhi Sultanate.

i18n.hi: प्रतापरुद्र सालों से सिंचित, दौलतमंद राज्य पर राज कर रहा था। हीरे वाली ज़मीनें और मंदिरों के ख़ज़ाने ने वरंगल को नकदी-प्यासे दिल्ली सल्तनत के लिए लज़ीज़ शिकार बना दिया था

panels.shot: close-up on Prataparudra’s face as he listens to distant drums
panels.action: A faint tremor runs through the stone floor as war drums thud outside; Prataparudra turns his head slightly, jaw clenched, listening.

dialogue.speaker: prataparudra_ii
dialogue.text: The northern lion has come for our granaries and gems, not for faith.

i18n.hi: उत्तरी शेर हमारी कोठियों और रत्नों के लिए आया है, न कि धर्म के लिए

panels.shot: wide shot from the outer earthen rampart facing Delhi camp
panels.action: Warangal’s outer mud wall looms in the foreground; beyond its ditch, rows of Delhi tents, siege engines and horse-lines stretch to the horizon as smoke rises from their campfires.

dialogue.text: Kafur encamped around the outer earthwork, testing this unfamiliar ringed fort. Siege machines rolled forward; arrows flew; but Warangal’s walls held firm at first.

i18n.hi: काफ़ूर ने बाहरी मिट्टी के घेरे पर पड़ाव डाला, इस अनजाने घेरदार किले को परखा। घेराबंदी की मशीनें बढ़ीं, तीर चले, पर शुरू में वरंगल की दीवारें जमी रहीं

panels.shot: medium shot of defenders atop outer wall, Prataparudra present among them
panels.action: Prataparudra stands on the outer rampart with archers and spearmen, watching stones crash against the earthen wall while dust clouds billow between the two forces.

dialogue.text: The hardened mud ramparts, raised by earlier Kakatiya kings, absorbed blows. Behind them, the stone fort and moat waited, a second line if the earth failed.

i18n.hi: काकतीय राजाओं ने पहले बनवाई ये सख़्त मिट्टी की परकोटे, जो वार सहती रहीं। इनके पीछे पत्थर का किला और खाई तैयार थे—मिट्टी टूटे तो दूसरी दीवार

panels.shot: slow push-in on parched field and wilting crops beyond the fort
panels.action: Beyond the encircled walls, dry fields and withering crops lie unattended, smoke from occasional skirmishes drifting over them under a blazing sun.

dialogue.text: As days stretched into weeks, fields outside could not be tended. Supplies inside were finite. A long siege would test not only walls, but stomachs and nerves.

i18n.hi: दिन हफ़्ते में बदल गए, बाहर की ज़मीनें बे-खेती रहीं। अंदर का राशन सीमित था। लम्बा घेरा दीवारों ही नहीं, पेट और हिम्मत भी आज़माता

panels.shot: interior shot of granary, near-empty baskets, Prataparudra inspecting
panels.action: Prataparudra walks through a stone granary inside the inner fort, touching woven baskets that are only half full, the air heavy and still.

dialogue.text: We do not have a day-by-day siege diary. Yet the strain is clear: surrounded by a vast host, Prataparudra had to balance honor with the survival of his people.

i18n.hi: हमारे पास रोज़-रोज़ की घेराबंदी की डायरी नहीं। पर तनाव साफ़ है—हज़ारों से घिरे प्रतापरुद्र को मान-सम्मान और जनता की जान के बीच संतुलन रखना था

panels.shot: medium shot in council, heated discussion implied
panels.action: In the council hall, generals argue, hands sharp in the air; Prataparudra sits slightly apart, fingers steepled, expression grave and inward.

dialogue.text: Some urged fighting to the last. Others pointed to Delhi’s numbers and the fort’s stores. The king listened, knowing each choice would mark his name in stone.

i18n.hi: कुछ ने आख़िरी साँस तक लड़ने को कहा। कुछ ने दिल्ली की तादाद और किले का राशन गिनाया। राजा सुनता रहा, जानता था हर फ़ैसला उसका नाम पत्थर पर लिख देगा

panels.shot: close-up of Prataparudra’s hand hovering over a map showing tribute routes
panels.action: On a palm-leaf map showing routes north, Prataparudra’s hand pauses over a line sketched toward the Ganga plains, then slowly closes into a fist.

dialogue.speaker: prataparudra_ii
dialogue.text: If treasure can buy time, we shall pay with gold, not blood.

i18n.hi: अगर ख़ज़ाना वक़्त खरीद सके, तो सोना देंगे, ख़ून नहीं

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle of Prataparudra atop inner stone fort looking out
panels.action: Standing on the highest stone bastion, Prataparudra looks beyond the moat toward the distant northern camp, his cloak stirring in the wind, guards behind him.

dialogue.text: Then, according to Khusrau, everything changed. Warangal’s king chose submission. Tribute would go to Delhi, and the siege would end without storming the inner stone fort.

i18n.hi: फिर, ख़ुसरो के मुताबिक सब बदल गया। वरंगल के राजा ने आत्मसमर्पण चुना। खंडणी दिल्ली जाएगी, और पत्थर के भीतर वाले किले पर तूफ़ानी हमला हुए बिना घेराबंदी खत्म होगी

panels.shot: medium shot of emissaries leaving the gate under white flag
panels.action: From a fortified gateway, Prataparudra’s emissaries ride out under a white cloth, guarded by Kakatiya horsemen, toward the lines of Delhi soldiers and banners.

dialogue.text: Envoys carried the king’s decision. Warangal would send elephants, horses and treasure to Alauddin Khalji, and in return, its ruler and city would be spared immediate conquest.

i18n.hi: दूतों ने राजा का फ़ैसला पहुँचाया। वरंगल अलाउद्दीन खिलज़ी को हाथी, घोड़े और ख़ज़ाना भेजेगा, और बदले में उसका राजा और शहर तुरंत फ़तह से बच जाएगा

panels.shot: wide shot of an inner courtyard piled with chests and tethered elephants
panels.action: In a stone courtyard, lines of elephants stand tethered, trunks swaying near heaps of wooden chests and bales, Kakatiya officials overseeing careful loading.

dialogue.text: Scholars note that Delhi hungered for such spoils. Warangal’s tribute fed Khalji campaigns and the Sultanate’s treasury, linking Deccan wealth to the politics of faraway Delhi.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकार कहते हैं दिल्ली ऐसे माल की भूखी थी। वरंगल की खंडणी ने खिलज़ी की मुहिमों और सल्तनत के ख़ज़ाने को ताक़त दी, दक्कन की दौलत को दूर दिल्ली की सियासत से जोड़ दिया

panels.shot: close-up on a jewelled casket being closed by attendants
panels.action: Hands of temple treasurers gently place large uncut stones and ornaments into a carved casket before shutting its heavy lid, lamplight gleaming on jewels.

dialogue.text: Among such riches were diamonds from southern mines. Later tradition ties the Koh-i-Noor to these treasuries, though no inscription names it here; its path to Delhi likely began around this era.

i18n.hi: इन दौलतों में दक्षिणी खानों के हीरे भी थे। बाद की परंपरा कोहिनूर को इन्हीं ख़ज़ानों से जोड़ती है, चाहे यहाँ कोई लिखित ज़िक्र नहीं; उसका सफ़र दिल्ली की तरफ़ शायद इसी दौर में शुरू हुआ

panels.shot: medium shot of Prataparudra overseeing departure from atop gate tower
panels.action: From a gate tower, Prataparudra watches the tribute caravan—elephants, horses, carts laden with chests—slowly filing out between the fort’s massive stone jambs.

dialogue.speaker: prataparudra_ii
dialogue.text: Let the wealth go. What matters is that Warangal wakes tomorrow.

i18n.hi: दौलत जाने दो। ज़रूरी ये है कि वरंगल कल सुबह ज़िंदा जागे

panels.shot: wide shot of Delhi camp striking tents and marching away
panels.action: Delhi soldiers dismantle tents and load gear; Kafur’s host turns from the fort and begins to move off across the plain as Warangal’s walls stand silent behind them.

dialogue.text: With tribute secured, Malik Kafur withdrew. Warangal’s granite heart was not breached in 1310. Prataparudra remained on his throne—for now.

i18n.hi: खंडणी तय होते ही मलिक काफ़ूर लौट गया। १३१० में वरंगल का ग्रेनाइट दिल नहीं टूटा। प्रतापरुद्र अभी अपने सिंहासन पर था

panels.shot: slow push-in on Prataparudra alone in a temple courtyard at dusk
panels.action: At dusk, Prataparudra stands in a quiet temple courtyard within the fort, stone pillars around him, lamps flickering as he looks up at the darkening sky.

dialogue.text: Later sieges and decline would still come. Yet at this first Delhi siege, Prataparudra chose to bend, not break—reminding us that in hard times, survival may demand surrendering even what seems most precious.

i18n.hi: बाद में और घेराबंदियाँ और पतन आएँगे। पर पहली दिल्ली घेराबंदी में प्रतापरुद्र ने झुकना चुना, टूटना नहीं—याद दिलाते हुए कि कठिन वक़्त में ज़िंदा रहना अक्सर सबसे क़ीमती चीज़ें छोड़ने की माँग करता है

title_i18n.hi: ग्रेनाइट की दीवारों पर मलिक काफ़ूर

subtitle_i18n.en: At Warangal’s Rings of Earth and Stone, a King Chooses Survival Over Glory
subtitle_i18n.hi: वरंगल की मिट्टी- पत्थर की अंगूठियों पर, एक राजा ने शोहरत नहीं, बचाव चुना
